review_notes: I read the whole file and the definitions of serrinSM, serrinKernel and serrinSM_eq_integral in PartV/SerrinSpaceTimeMollify.lean. I grepped for every use of serrinSM that unfolds it via simp or simpa, and I looked at the signatures of the CKN mollifier lemmas the file uses. I did not find simp-attribute problems such as loops or competing rules in this file, because it declares no simp lemmas. The one finding is about the missing slice-evaluation lemma for serrinSM. Whether the proposed lemma is `@[simp]` or just a `rw` lemma is a judgement call. I could not run Lean, so I have not checked that the suggested replacement compiles. I did not check how robust the current `simpa` calls are; the finding rests on how they are written.

findings.declaration: ESS.lps_mollify_mixed_norm_tendsto (simpa calls unfolding serrinSM / CKN.mollify / CKN.mollifier)
findings.problem: serrinSM has no canonical evaluation lemma. This proof bridges the slice-wise form `fun x => serrinSM f n (x,t)` to the CKN statements by unfolding three definitions inside `simpa`. That includes `CKN.mollifier`, which is the kernel construction. The same unfolding is repeated at line 144 as `simpa [N, serrinSM] using hconv`. Other files also unfold it as `simp only [serrinSM]` (CrossIdentityFour, MixedCrossIdentityAssembly, SerrinCrossIdentity). Unfolding the kernel definition is an unwanted expansion and makes the result depend on how simp normalises those internals. The result is a fragile, unstable simp set. The one existing lemma, `serrinSM_eq_integral`, goes to an integral, which is not the form these call sites need.
findings.proposed_change: Next to the definition of serrinSM, add a slice lemma, e.g. `theorem serrinSM_apply (f) (n) (x : Vec3) (t : ℝ) : serrinSM f n (x, t) = CKN.mollify (fun y : Vec3 => f (y, t)) (serrinRadius n) (serrinRadius_pos n) x := rfl`. Optionally mark it `@[simp]`. Its direction is safe because it only exposes `CKN.mollify` and does not unfold it further. Then replace line 121 by `simpa [serrinSM_apply, CKN.mollify] using hmol`, or by a `rw` with it, which drops `CKN.mollifier`. Replace line 144 by `simpa [N, serrinSM_apply] using hconv`. The other files can use the same lemma in place of `simp only [serrinSM]`.
findings.benefit: There is one stable rewrite rule for the slice-wise form, so call sites do not unfold the kernel definition. The proofs no longer depend on how `CKN.mollifier` is unfolded and are less likely to break if the mollifier definition changes. The multiple files that currently unfold the definition get a single named rule.
